messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU pool 'us-west2-spot' >=95% utilization; request queue length 124; preemptible interruption spike detected. Severity: P1. Pager duty routed to maria.

maria (oncall): Acknowledged. Creating a bridge. @kevin @lee can you join? Sharing logs and quick summary in thread.

kevin: joining. first look — autoscaler hit max_nodes=40, attempts to scale beyond are failing with cloud errors. I'm pulling cluster autoscaler and pool state.

lee: we see a burst of preemptions — roughly 48 preempt events in the last 6m. Many pods in Terminating state waiting for PV detach. KV-cache warms lost for several models, causing long tails.

maria (oncall): Sara, any customer-facing errors showing up?

sara: support: yes, we're seeing elevated 503s and timeouts for generation endpoints for customers 'api-corp' and 'fastchat'. Example trace: 503 from route /v1/generate -> backend: gpu-queue-timeout. Posting ticket links.

kevin: looking at autoscaler logs: 

```
I0912 21:04:12 autoscaler.go:221] Desired=45, Max=40, ScaleUpFailed: Insufficient capacity
Error: provider returned Insufficient capacity error
```

kevin: provider quota isn't the issue — it's actual capacity shortage. Cloud returning capacity errors for spot GPUs.

dave (infra): Confirmed from cloud metrics: unusual spot eviction cadence in us-west2 due to maintenance window + regional demand. Reserved pool only has 4 free GPUs, not enough to absorb. I've opened an urgent ticket with provider (INC-12345).

maria (oncall): Ok. Immediate mitigations we can do: 1) throttle low-priority / background eval queues, 2) temporarily route some traffic to us-east1, 3) disable new spot allocations for demand-heavy routes, 4) try to expand reserved/dedicated pool if provider offers. Kevin/Lee run those.

kevin: applying configuration change: set scheduler poolSelector -> prefer:reserved then spot for new requests. Pushing change now.

lee: attempting manual reserved pool scale to +4 GPUs. Cloud API returns 'Insufficient capacity in zone'. Trying cross-zone allocation to us-west2-b -> fails as well.

raj: I'm applying a global throttle for non-SLA traffic. Command: 

```
curl -X POST https://ops-api.internal/queues/throttle -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' -d '{"scope":"low-priority","rate":0.1}'
```

raj: throttle request submitted.

ops-bot: Throttle applied: low-priority queues -> 10% of usual throughput.

kevin: deploying smart routing rule 'region-fallback' to send ~20% of generation requests to us-east1 (where capacity currently available). Applying in 30s.

incident-bot: Bridge created: https://meet.example/bridge/2123456789. Provider ticket INC-12345 opened.

maria (oncall): Sara, notify highest-affected customers and mark incident active. Use the incident template.

sara: Support update posted for api-corp and fastchat. Notifying account reps. Customers confirmed degraded, appreciate update.

dave (infra): Provider responded: capacity tight in us-west2 for next ~2 hours, suggested use cross-region or reserved instances. They offered no immediate spare capacity.

kevin: reroute applied; traffic shift in progress. Early metrics: queue length dropping from 124 -> 62 over 6 minutes. Latency 95p improving.

maria (oncall): Next actions: keep throttles in place for low-priority until stable, continue reroute, keep provider ticket open, and prepare to spin up dedicated reserve if spot remains unavailable. Also create post-incident follow-ups: increase reserved pool size, add autoscaler guardrails to avoid hard maxing to insufficient nodes, and ensure per-customer fallback policies.

lee: manual reserved spin succeeded for +2 GPUs (from a secondary zone). That gives us breathing room. Trying to gracefully drain Terminating pods and warm caches.

ops-bot: Metrics update — queue length: 32, active nodes: 42, preempt events in last 10m: 12.

maria (oncall): Good. Handoff plan: I need to sign out at 22:00 UTC. @lee you'll take the active oncall. Lee, confirm you'll monitor until queue stable < 20 and customer errors resolved.

lee: Acknowledged. I'll monitor the bridge and metrics. Will continue throttles and reroute until we have sustained capacity.

sara: Support: customers 'api-corp' and 'fastchat' report partial recovery; tickets updated. Will keep wave notifications until full recovery.

kevin: quick temp runbook note I'm adding now: if autoscaler Desired > Max_nodes and provider returns Insufficient capacity, then: 1) auto-apply low-prio throttle, 2) enable cross-region fallback, 3) enable reserved pool burst if available, 4) escalate to infra. I'll open a PR for permanent runbook changes.

maria (oncall): Leaving channel for handoff. Postmortem owners: kevin (autoscaling fixes), lee (runtime hardening), dave (provider liaison), sara (customer comms). Please file a postmortem within 48h.

incident-bot: Pager duty note: alert closed for maria; reassigned to lee.

lee: Confirming last state before primary signout — queue 18, 503s back to baseline, provider ticket still open but we've mitigated customer impact. I'll keep monitoring and escalate if degradation returns.

maria (oncall): Thanks team. :thumbsup: Pinning this thread for the postmortem and runbook PRs.

kevin: Follow-ups I'll open: PR to increase autoscaler headroom, runbook PR for spot-preempt failure mode, and an alert to detect repeated Insufficient capacity responses.

sara: I'll follow up on customer tickets and post a short status once provider confirms long-term capacity plan.

dave (infra): Noting provider suggested long-term mitigation: reserve minimal dedicated pool for critical SLAs. Will put proposal on infra board.

ops-bot: Channel archived from active bridge at 21:47 UTC.

lee: Closing active mitigation. Will convene postmortem tomorrow.

support-bot: Incident log saved to /incidents/2123456789 for postmortem reference.
